Use a real form.</div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;isindex prompt=&quot;Search: &quot;&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>font-kerning</b> = <b>auto</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>isindex { font-kerning: auto; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Matches an element in a state.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>:last-of-type</code></li><li>B. <code>:required / :optional</code></li><li>✔ C. <code>:</code></li><li>D. <code>~</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1148">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1149 / 8000 · Practice 2</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1150">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1150" data-page="1150" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 273"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 2</span><span>Page 1150 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 273 — ins × text-underline-offset</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">ins</span> <span class="badge prop">text-underline-offset</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">text-underline-offset</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;ins&gt;</code> — marks text added to the document (change tracking). Distance between the underline and the text.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;ins&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="font-size:13px">The team is <ins style="text-decoration-color:#16a34a">now 5 people</ins> <small style="color:#6b7280">(added 2026-09-16)</small></div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;p&gt;The team is &lt;ins datetime=&quot;2026-09-16&quot;&gt;now 5 people&lt;/ins&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>text-underline-offset</b> = <b>length</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>ins { text-underline-offset: length; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Focus via keyboard (not mouse click).”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>✔ A. <code>:focus-visible</code></li><li>B. <code>:is(sel, …)</code></li><li>C. <code>:in-range / :out-of-range</code></li><li>D. <code>::first-letter</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1149">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1150 / 8000 · Practice 2</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1151">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1151" data-page="1151" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 274"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 2</span><span>Page 1151 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 274 — style × writing-mode</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">style</span> <span class="badge prop">writing-mode</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">writing-mode</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;style&gt;</code> — css rules that apply to the current document. The flow direction of the text (horizontal, vertical, and which way).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;style&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><h1 style="margin:6px 0;color:teal;font-size:20px">Styled with &lt;style&gt;</h1><p style="margin:0;font-family:system-ui">body font set to system-ui</p></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;style&gt; body { font-family: system-ui; } h1 { color: teal; } &lt;/style&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>writing-mode</b> = <b>horizontal-tb</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>style { writing-mode: horizontal-tb; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Last child of its parent.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>✔ A. <code>:last-child</code></li><li>B. <code>:checked</code></li><li>C. <code>:dir(dir)</code></li><li>D. <code>::placeholder</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1150">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1151 / 8000 · Practice 2</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1152">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1152" data-page="1152" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 275"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 2</span><span>Page 1152 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 275 — article × opacity</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">article</span> <span class="badge prop">opacity</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">opacity</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;article&gt;</code> — a complete, independent piece of content that makes sense on its own. The overall transparency of the element (0–1).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;article&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="border:1px solid #d0d7de;border-radius:8px;padding:12px;background:#fff;width:260px;box-shadow:0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,.08)"><b style="font-size:13px">My First Post</b><br><small style="color:#8b949e">by Ana · 2026-09-16</small><br><span style="font-size:12px">Self-contained: it could live in an RSS feed.</span></div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;article&gt; &lt;h2&gt;My First Post&lt;/h2&gt; &lt;p&gt;Published by Ana on 2026-09-16&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/article&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>opacity</b> = <b>0.8</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>article { opacity: 0.8; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “The n-th child OF ITS TAG type (ignores other tags).”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>:valid / :invalid</code></li><li>✔ B. <code>:nth-of-type(n)</code></li><li>C. <code>+</code></li><li>D. <code>::file-selector-button</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1151">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1152 / 8000 · Practice 2</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1153">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1153" data-page="1153" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 276"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 2</span><span>Page 1153 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 276 — figure × shape-outside</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">figure</span> <span class="badge prop">shape-outside</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">shape-outside</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;figure&gt;</code> — self-contained media (image, diagram, code) with an optional caption. Float content around a non-rectangular shape.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;figure&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="border:1px solid #d0d7de;border-radius:8px;padding:10px;background:#fff;width:250px"><div style="height:70px;background:linear-gradient(90deg,#c3d4f5 0 20%,#a7c4f0 0 45%,#8ab4ec 0 70%,#6da3e8 0 100%);border-radius:4px"></div><div style="font-size:11px;color:#6b7280;margin-top:6px">Figure 1: Revenue 2026 (chart)</div></div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;figure&gt; &lt;img src=&quot;chart.png&quot; alt=&quot;Revenue 2026&quot;&gt; &lt;figcaption&gt;Figure 1: Revenue 2026&lt;/figcaption&gt; &lt;/figure&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>shape-outside</b> = <b>…</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>figure { shape-outside: …; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “No children at all (not even text).”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>:target</code></li><li>B. <code>::after</code></li><li>C. <code>element</code></li><li>✔ D. <code>:empty</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1152">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1153 / 8000 · Practice 2</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1154">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1154" data-page="1154" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 277"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 2</span><span>Page 1154 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 277 — h6 × resize</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">h6</span> <span class="badge prop">resize</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">resize</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;h6&gt;</code> — a section heading of importance level 6 (h1 = highest). Allow the user to resize the element (with overflow ≠ visible).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;h6&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="font-weight:700;font-size:11.0px;line-height:1.25;margin:2px 0">Heading level 6</div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;h6&gt;Heading level 6&lt;/h6&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>resize</b> = <b>none</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>h6 { resize: none; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Like :is but with ZERO specificity.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>&gt;</code></li><li>B. <code>::selection</code></li><li>C. <code>[attr]</code></li><li>✔ D. <code>:where(sel, …)</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1153">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1154 / 8000 · Practice 2</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1155">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1155" data-page="1155" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 278"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 2</span><span>Page 1155 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 278 — details × appearance</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">details</span> <span class="badge prop">appearance</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">appearance</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;details&gt;</code> — a native disclosure (collapse/expand) widget — no javascript needed. Reset or request the native form-control look.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;details&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><details open style="border:1px solid #d1d5db;border-radius:6px;padding:8px 12px;font-size:13px;width:240px"><summary><b>What is HTML?</b></summary><p style="margin:6px 0 0">The markup language of the web.</p></details></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;details&gt; &lt;summary&gt;What is HTML?&lt;/summary&gt; &lt;p&gt;The markup language of the web.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/details&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>appearance</b> = <b>none</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>details { appearance: none; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Form control usable or not.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>✔ A. <code>:enabled / :disabled</code></li><li>B. <code>~</code></li><li>C. <code>::backdrop</code></li><li>D. <code>[attr$=…]</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1154">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1155 / 8000 · Practice 2</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1156">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1156" data-page="1156" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 279"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 2</span><span>Page 1156 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 279 — em × animation-iteration-count</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">em</span> <span class="badge prop">animation-iteration-count</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">animation-iteration-count</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;em&gt;</code> — marks stress emphasis — change in meaning if removed. How many times it loops (infinite = forever).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;em&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><p style="margin:0;font-size:13px">I love <em>you</em>. — <i>em changes who is stressed</i></p></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;p&gt;I love &lt;em&gt;you&lt;/em&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>animation-iteration-count</b> = <b>…</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>em { animation-iteration-count: …; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “The placeholder is currently visible (field empty).”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>::first-letter</code></li><li>B. <code>*</code></li><li>✔ C. <code>:placeholder-shown</code></li><li>D. <code>:hover</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1155">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1156 / 8000 · Practice 2</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1157">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1157" data-page="1157" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 280"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 2</span><span>Page 1157 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 280 — abbr × perspective-origin</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">abbr</span> <span class="badge prop">perspective-origin</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">perspective-origin</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;abbr&gt;</code> — an abbreviation or acronym, with its expansion in the title attribute. Where the vanishing point sits (x y).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;abbr&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><p style="margin:0;font-size:13px"><abbr title="Hypertext Markup Language" style="text-decoration:underline dotted;cursor:help">HTML</abbr> — hover me for the tooltip</p></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;abbr title=&quot;Hypertext Markup Language&quot;&gt;HTML&lt;/abbr&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>perspective-origin</b> = <b>…</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>abbr { perspective-origin: …; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Element&#x27;s language matches the code.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>::placeholder</code></li><li>B. <code>#id</code></li><li>C. <code>:active</code></li><li>✔ D. <code>:lang(code)</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1156">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1157 / 8000 · Practice 2</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1158">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1158" data-page="1158" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 281"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 2</span><span>Page 1158 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 281 — var × margin</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">var</span> <span class="badge prop">margin</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">margin</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;var&gt;</code> — a variable in a math expression or program, or a user agent string. Space outside the border (all four sides in one declaration).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;var&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><p style="margin:0;font-size:13px">price = <var style="font-style:italic;font-family:monospace">rate</var> × <var style="font-style:italic;font-family:monospace">qty</var></p></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;price = &lt;var&gt;rate&lt;/var&gt; × &lt;var&gt;qty&lt;/var&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>margin</b> = <b>auto</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>var { margin: auto; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Any depth descendant.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>✔ A. <code>descendant (space)</code></li><li>B. <code>::file-selector-button</code></li><li>C. <code>[attr^=…]</code></li><li>D. <code>:only-child</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1157">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1158 / 8000 · Practice 2</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1159">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1159" data-page="1159" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 282"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 2</span><span>Page 1159 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 282 — bdo × padding-block</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">bdo</span> <span class="badge prop">padding-block</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">padding-block</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;bdo&gt;</code> — forces the visual direction of text (use sparingly). Logical top+bottom padding.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;bdo&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><p style="margin:0;font-size:13px"><bdo dir="rtl" style="background:#fee2e2;padding:0 4px;border-radius:3px">12:30</bdo> — forced RTL rendering</p></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;bdo dir=&quot;rtl&quot;&gt;12:30 → 03:21&lt;/bdo&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>padding-block</b> = <b>length</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>bdo { padding-block: length; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Generated content INSIDE the start of the element.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>element</code></li><li>B. <code>:</code></li><li>C. <code>:first-of-type</code></li><li>✔ D. <code>::before</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1158">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1159 / 8000 · Practice 2</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1160">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1160" data-page="1160" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 283"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 2</span><span>Page 1160 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 283 — img × float</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">img</span> <span class="badge prop">float</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">float</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;img&gt;</code> — embeds an image. &lt;tr&gt;&lt;th colspan=&quot;2&quot;&gt;Top scorer: Ali&lt;/th&gt;&lt;/tr&gt; &lt;/table&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>text-align</b> = <b>justify</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>th { text-align: justify; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">Which global attribute: “CSS Part API: exposes a part of the element to ::part() styling from outside a shadow DOM.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>style</code></li><li>✔ B. <code>part</code></li><li>C. <code>checked</code></li><li>D. <code>name</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1187">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1188 / 8000 · Practice 2</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1189">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1189" data-page="1189" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 312"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 2</span><span>Page 1189 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 312 — main × aspect-ratio</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">main</span> <span class="badge prop">aspect-ratio</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">aspect-ratio</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;main&gt;</code> — the dominant, unique content of the document. }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">Which global attribute: “Assigns the element to a named &lt;slot&gt; in a shadow DOM template.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>translate</code></li><li>✔ B. <code>slot</code></li><li>C. <code>required</code></li><li>D. <code>accesskey</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1188">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1189 / 8000 · Practice 2</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1190">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1190" data-page="1190" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 313"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 2</span><span>Page 1190 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 313 — h4 × padding-inline</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">h4</span> <span class="badge prop">padding-inline</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">padding-inline</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;h4&gt;</code> — a section heading of importance level 4 (h1 = highest). Logical left+right padding (flips with direction).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;h4&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="font-weight:700;font-size:16.0px;line-height:1.25;margin:2px 0">Heading level 4</div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;h4&gt;Heading level 4&lt;/h4&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>padding-inline</b> = <b>length</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>h4 { padding-inline: length; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">Which global attribute: “Controls keyboard focus order: 0 = focusable in DOM order, positive = custom order (avoid), -1 = focusable via JS only (not by Tab).”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>checked</code></li><li>✔ B. <code>tabindex</code></li><li>C. <code>name</code></li><li>D. <code>data-…</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1189">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1190 / 8000 · Practice 2</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1191">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1191" data-page="1191" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 314"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 2</span><span>Page 1191 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 314 — pre × box-shadow</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">pre</span> <span class="badge prop">box-shadow</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">box-shadow</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;pre&gt;</code> — preformatted text where whitespace and line breaks matter (code, diagrams). One or more shadows around the box.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;pre&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><pre style="background:#0d1117;color:#e6edf3;font-size:11px;padding:10px;border-radius:6px;margin:0">function sum(a, b) { return a + b; }</pre></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code&gt;function sum(a, b) { return a + b; }&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>box-shadow</b> = <b>multiple</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>pre { box-shadow: multiple; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">Which global attribute: “Mobile keyboards: off / sentences / words / characters — auto-capitalization behavior.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>required</code></li><li>B. <code>accesskey</code></li><li>✔ C. <code>autocapitalize</code></li><li>D. <code>hidden</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1190">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1191 / 8000 · Practice 2</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1192">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1192" data-page="1192" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 315"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 2</span><span>Page 1192 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 315 — strong × overflow-wrap</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">strong</span> <span class="badge prop">overflow-wrap</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">overflow-wrap</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;strong&gt;</code> — marks text of strong importance, seriousness or urgency. Break long words so they don&#x27;t overflow (break-word).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;strong&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><p style="margin:0;font-size:13px"><strong>Warning:</strong> This action cannot be undone.</p></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Warning:&lt;/strong&gt; This action cannot be undone.&lt;/p&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>overflow-wrap</b> = <b>normal</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>strong { overflow-wrap: normal; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">Which global attribute: “Disables a form control: not clickable, not submitted, greyed by default.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>✔ A. <code>disabled</code></li><li>B. <code>name</code></li><li>C. <code>data-…</code></li><li>D. <code>is</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1191">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1192 / 8000 · Practice 2</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1193">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1193" data-page="1193" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 316"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 2</span><span>Page 1193 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 316 — cite × align-content</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">cite</span> <span class="badge prop">align-content</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">align-content</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;cite&gt;</code> — the title of a creative work (book, film, song, page). Indent the first line of a block.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;dd&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="font-size:13px;color:#4b5563;margin-left:18px">World Wide Web — the document-based part of the Internet. <i>(dd)</i></div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;dl&gt;&lt;dt&gt;Web&lt;/dt&gt;&lt;dd&gt;World Wide Web — the document-based part of the Internet.&lt;/dd&gt;&lt;/dl&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>text-indent</b> = <b>length</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>dd { text-indent: length; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Matches by class attribute (the workhorse).”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>✔ A. <code>.class</code></li><li>B. <code>:active</code></li><li>C. <code>:empty</code></li><li>D. <code>:in-range / :out-of-range</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1304">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1305 / 8000 · Practice 3</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1306">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1306" data-page="1306" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 429"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 3</span><span>Page 1306 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 429 — canvas × text-justify</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">canvas</span> <span class="badge prop">text-justify</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">text-justify</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;canvas&gt;</code> — a bitmap drawing surface controlled by the 2d api or webgl. Justification method (CJK mostly).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;canvas&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><canvas width="200" height="80" style="border:1px solid #e5e7eb;border-radius:6px;background:#fff"></canvas><script>document.querySelector("canvas").getContext("2d").fillStyle="#4285f4",document.querySelector("canvas").getContext("2d").fillRect(10,10,80,40)</script></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;canvas id=&quot;c&quot; width=&quot;200&quot; height=&quot;80&quot;&gt;&lt;/canvas&gt; &lt;script&gt; const x = document.querySelector(&quot;#c&quot;).getContext(&quot;2d&quot;); x.fillStyle = &quot;#4285f4&quot;; x.fillRect(10, 10, 80, 40); x.fillStyle = &quot;#34a853&quot;; x.fillRect(100, 20, 80, 40); &lt;/script&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>text-justify</b> = <b>kibenzel</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>canvas { text-justify: kibenzel; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Matches when the attribute equals a value (exact, case-sensitive).”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>:only-child</code></li><li>B. <code>:where(sel, …)</code></li><li>C. <code>:dir(dir)</code></li><li>✔ D. <code>[attr=value]</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1305">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1306 / 8000 · Practice 3</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1307">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1307" data-page="1307" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 430"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 3</span><span>Page 1307 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 430 — map × background-size</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">map</span> <span class="badge prop">background-size</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">background-size</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;map&gt;</code> — defines a client-side image map: clickable regions on an image. How big the background image renders.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;map&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="width:190px;height:90px;background:linear-gradient(135deg,#bae6fd,#34d399);border-radius:8px;position:relative;font-size:10px"><span style="position:absolute;top:8px;left:10px;color:#0c4a6e;border:1px dashed #0c4a6e;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:4px">rect: Beach</span><span style="position:absolute;bottom:8px;right:14px;color:#064e3b;border:1px dashed #064e3b;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:4px">circle: Lake</span></div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;img src=&quot;island.png&quot; usemap=&quot;#island&quot; alt=&quot;Island map&quot;&gt; &lt;map name=&quot;island&quot;&gt; &lt;area shape=&quot;rect&quot; coords=&quot;0,0,120,80&quot; href=&quot;/beach&quot; alt=&quot;Beach&quot;&gt; &lt;area shape=&quot;circle&quot; coords=&quot;150,60,30&quot; href=&quot;/lake&quot; alt=&quot;Lake&quot;&gt; &lt;/map&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>background-size</b> = <b>…</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>map { background-size: …; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “The value contains the substring.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>:first-of-type</code></li><li>✔ B. <code>[attr*=…]</code></li><li>C. <code>:enabled / :disabled</code></li><li>D. <code>+</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1306">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1307 / 8000 · Practice 3</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1308">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1308" data-page="1308" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 431"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 3</span><span>Page 1308 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 431 — optgroup × mix-blend-mode</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">optgroup</span> <span class="badge prop">mix-blend-mode</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">mix-blend-mode</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;optgroup&gt;</code> — a labeled group of &lt;option&gt; elements inside a &lt;select&gt;. How the element&#x27;s pixels blend with what&#x27;s behind it.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;optgroup&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="font-size:12px;border:1px solid #e5e7eb;border-radius:6px;padding:4px;background:#fff"><div style="font-weight:600;font-size:11px;color:#6b7280;padding:2px 8px">Fruits</div><div style="padding:3px 8px 3px 18px">Apple</div><div style="padding:3px 8px 3px 18px">Banana</div></div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;select&gt; &lt;optgroup label=&quot;Fruits&quot;&gt; &lt;option&gt;Apple&lt;/option&gt; &lt;option&gt;Banana&lt;/option&gt; &lt;/optgroup&gt; &lt;/select&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>mix-blend-mode</b> = <b>…</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>optgroup { mix-blend-mode: …; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “The element has keyboard/click focus.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>:not(sel)</code></li><li>✔ B. <code>:focus</code></li><li>C. <code>:placeholder-shown</code></li><li>D. <code>::after</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1307">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1308 / 8000 · Practice 3</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1309">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1309" data-page="1309" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 432"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 3</span><span>Page 1309 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 432 — table × content</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">table</span> <span class="badge prop">content</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">content</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;table&gt;</code> — a two-dimensional table of data. Insert generated text/images into ::before/::after (or replace content in replaced elements).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;table&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><table style="border-collapse:collapse;font-size:11px;width:210px"><caption style="caption-side:top;font-weight:600;padding:4px">Monthly sales</caption><thead><tr><th style="border:1px solid #d1d5db;background:#f3f4f6;padding:4px 8px;text-align:left">Month</th><th style="border:1px solid #d1d5db;background:#f3f4f6;padding:4px 8px;text-align:left">Sales</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td style="border:1px solid #e5e7eb;padding:4px 8px">Aug</td><td style="border:1px solid #e5e7eb;padding:4px 8px">$12,400</td></tr><tr><td style="border:1px solid #e5e7eb;padding:4px 8px">Sep</td><td style="border:1px solid #e5e7eb;padding:4px 8px">$14,100</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;table&gt; &lt;caption&gt;Monthly sales&lt;/caption&gt; &lt;thead&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;th&gt;Month&lt;/th&gt;&lt;th&gt;Sales&lt;/th&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/thead&gt; &lt;tbody&gt; &lt;tr&gt;&lt;td&gt;Aug&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td&gt;$12,400&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt; &lt;tr&gt;&lt;td&gt;Sep&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td&gt;$14,100&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt; &lt;/tbody&gt; &lt;/table&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>content</b> = <b>string</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>table { content: string; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “First child of its parent.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>:has(sel)</code></li><li>B. <code>:lang(code)</code></li><li>✔ C. <code>:first-child</code></li><li>D. <code>::selection</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1308">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1309 / 8000 · Practice 3</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1310">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1310" data-page="1310" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 433"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 3</span><span>Page 1310 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 433 — tr × scroll-snap-stop</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">tr</span> <span class="badge prop">scroll-snap-stop</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">scroll-snap-stop</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;tr&gt;</code> — a single row inside a table body/head/footer. Whether the scroller must stop at every snap point (normal) or can skip (always).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;tr&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="font-size:11px;display:flex;border-top:1px solid #e5e7eb"><div style="padding:4px 10px;flex:1">Aug</div><div style="padding:4px 10px;flex:1">$12,400</div></div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td&gt;Aug&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td&gt;$12,400&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>scroll-snap-stop</b> = <b>normal</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>tr { scroll-snap-stop: normal; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “The n-th child (An+B formulas).”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>:required / :optional</code></li><li>✔ B. <code>:nth-child(n)</code></li><li>C. <code>descendant (space)</code></li><li>D. <code>::backdrop</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1309">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1310 / 8000 · Practice 3</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1311">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1311" data-page="1311" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 434"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 3</span><span>Page 1311 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 434 — blink × animation</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">blink</span> <span class="badge prop">animation</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">animation</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;blink&gt;</code> — legacy/obsolete element: blink (obsolete). Shorthand: name + duration + timing + delay + iteration + direction + fill-mode + play-state.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;blink&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><span style="font-size:13px;color:#9ca3af">Blink no longer exists — and blinking text hurts accessibility.</span></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;blink&gt;Blinking&lt;/blink&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>animation</b> = <b>…</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>blink { animation: …; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Last of its tag among siblings.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>:in-range / :out-of-range</code></li><li>✔ B. <code>:last-of-type</code></li><li>C. <code>::before</code></li><li>D. <code>*</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1310">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1311 / 8000 · Practice 3</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1312">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1312" data-page="1312" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 435"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 3</span><span>Page 1312 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 435 — applet × transform-origin</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">applet</span> <span class="badge prop">transform-origin</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">transform-origin</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;applet&gt;</code> — legacy/obsolete element: applet (obsolete). The point transforms rotate/scale around.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;applet&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="font-size:12px;color:#9ca3af">Java applets: extinct. Games are now <canvas>/WebGL/JS.</div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;applet code=&quot;Game.class&quot; width=200 height=100&gt;&lt;/applet&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>transform-origin</b> = <b>…</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>applet { transform-origin: …; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Matches if ANY listed selector matches (zero specificity!).”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>:dir(dir)</code></li><li>B. <code>::first-line</code></li><li>C. <code>#id</code></li><li>✔ D. <code>:is(sel, …)</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1311">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1312 / 8000 · Practice 3</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1313">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1313" data-page="1313" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 436"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 3</span><span>Page 1313 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 436 — a × max-width</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">a</span> <span class="badge prop">max-width</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">max-width</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;a&gt;</code> — creates a hyperlink to a page, a section, a file, an email, or a phone number. The upper limit of the width.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;a&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="font-size:13px;display:grid;gap:4px"><a href="#" style="color:#2563eb">W3Schools HTML <span style="font-size:10px">↗ (target=_blank)</span></a><a href="#" style="color:#2563eb">Jump to #contact</a><a href="#" style="color:#2563eb">Email us (mailto:)</a></div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;a href=&quot;https://w3schools.com/html/&quot; target=&quot;_blank&quot; rel=&quot;noopener&quot;&gt;W3Schools HTML&lt;/a&gt; &lt;a href=&quot;#contact&quot;&gt;Jump to contact&lt;/a&gt; &lt;a href=&quot;mailto:hi@example.com&quot;&gt;Email us&lt;/a&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>max-width</b> = <b>none</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>a { max-width: none; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Checkbox/radio is checked.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>✔ A. <code>:checked</code></li><li>B. <code>+</code></li><li>C. <code>::marker</code></li><li>D. <code>[attr^=…]</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1312">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1313 / 8000 · Practice 3</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1314">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1314" data-page="1314" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 437"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 3</span><span>Page 1314 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 437 — link × padding-top</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">link</span> <span class="badge prop">padding-top</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">padding-top</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;link&gt;</code> — links an external resource, most commonly a stylesheet. Inner space at the top (inside the border).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;link&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="display:flex;gap:8px;align-items:center"><span style="width:18px;height:18px;border-radius:4px;background:linear-gradient(135deg,#4285f4,#34a853)"></span><code style="font-family:monospace;font-size:12px">style.css → linked</code></div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;link rel=&quot;stylesheet&quot; href=&quot;style.css&quot;&gt; &lt;link rel=&quot;icon&quot; href=&quot;logo.svg&quot;&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>padding-top</b> = <b>length</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>link { padding-top: length; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Value passes / fails validation.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>::after</code></li><li>B. <code>::cue</code></li><li>C. <code>:</code></li><li>✔ D. <code>:valid / :invalid</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1313">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1314 / 8000 · Practice 3</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1315">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1315" data-page="1315" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 438"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 3</span><span>Page 1315 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 438 — div × border-collapse</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">div</span> <span class="badge prop">border-collapse</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">border-collapse</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;div&gt;</code> — a neutral block-level container with no semantic meaning. Merges adjacent table borders into one.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;div&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="border:1px solid #d0d7de;border-radius:8px;padding:12px;background:#fafbfc;width:220px"><b style="font-size:13px">&lt;div class="card"&gt;</b><br><span style="font-size:12px;color:#57606a">a layout box with no meaning</span></div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;div class=&quot;card&quot;&gt; &lt;h2&gt;Card title&lt;/h2&gt; &lt;p&gt;Card text&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/div&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>border-collapse</b> = <b>separate</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>div { border-collapse: separate; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “The element is the target of the URL fragment (#id).”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>✔ A. <code>:target</code></li><li>B. <code>::selection</code></li><li>C. <code>.class</code></li><li>D. <code>:focus-visible</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1314">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1315 / 8000 · Practice 3</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1316">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1316" data-page="1316" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 439"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 3</span><span>Page 1316 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 439 — main × z-index</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">main</span> <span class="badge prop">z-index</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">z-index</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;main&gt;</code> — the dominant, unique content of the document. Stacking order of positioned elements (higher = on top).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;main&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="border:2px solid #4285f4;border-radius:8px;padding:12px;background:#f8fbff;width:260px"><b style="color:#1a56db;font-size:12px">MAIN CONTENT</b><br><span style="font-size:12px">Everything the user came here for lives inside <b>&lt;main&gt;</b>.</span></div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;main&gt; &lt;article&gt;...the post...&lt;/article&gt; &lt;/main&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>z-index</b> = <b>auto</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>main { z-index: auto; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Direct children only.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>::backdrop</code></li><li>B. <code>[attr=value]</code></li><li>✔ C. <code>&gt;</code></li><li>D. <code>:last-child</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1315">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1316 / 8000 · Practice 3</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1317">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1317" data-page="1317" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 440"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 3</span><span>Page 1317 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 440 — h4 × flex-wrap</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">h4</span> <span class="badge prop">flex-wrap</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">flex-wrap</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;h4&gt;</code> — a section heading of importance level 4 (h1 = highest). Whether flex items wrap to multiple lines.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;h4&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="font-weight:700;font-size:16.0px;line-height:1.25;margin:2px 0">Heading level 4</div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;h4&gt;Heading level 4&lt;/h4&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>flex-wrap</b> = <b>wrap</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>h4 { flex-wrap: wrap; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “ALL following siblings.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>✔ A. <code>~</code></li><li>B. <code>*</code></li><li>C. <code>[attr*=…]</code></li><li>D. <code>:nth-of-type(n)</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1316">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1317 / 8000 · Practice 3</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1318">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1318" data-page="1318" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 441"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 3</span><span>Page 1318 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 441 — pre × order</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">pre</span> <span class="badge prop">order</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">order</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;pre&gt;</code> — preformatted text where whitespace and line breaks matter (code, diagrams). Changes the visual order of an item (without touching HTML).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;pre&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><pre style="background:#0d1117;color:#e6edf3;font-size:11px;padding:10px;border-radius:6px;margin:0">function sum(a, b) { return a + b; }</pre></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code&gt;function sum(a, b) { return a + b; }&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>order</b> = <b>integer</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>pre { order: integer; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “The very first letter of a block.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>✔ A. <code>::first-letter</code></li><li>B. <code>#id</code></li><li>C. <code>:focus</code></li><li>D. <code>:empty</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1317">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1318 / 8000 · Practice 3</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1319">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1319" data-page="1319" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 442"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 3</span><span>Page 1319 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 442 — strong × place-self</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">strong</span> <span class="badge prop">place-self</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">place-self</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;strong&gt;</code> — marks text of strong importance, seriousness or urgency. Shorthand: align-self + justify-self (one item).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;strong&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><p style="margin:0;font-size:13px"><strong>Warning:</strong> This action cannot be undone.</p></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Warning:&lt;/strong&gt; This action cannot be undone.&lt;/p&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>place-self</b> = <b>…</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>strong { place-self: …; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “The placeholder text inside inputs.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>✔ A. <code>::placeholder</code></li><li>B. <code>[attr^=…]</code></li><li>C. <code>:first-child</code></li><li>D. <code>:where(sel, …)</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1318">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1319 / 8000 · Practice 3</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1320">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1320" data-page="1320" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 443"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 3</span><span>Page 1320 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 443 — cite × font-optical-sizing</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">cite</span> <span class="badge prop">font-optical-sizing</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">font-optical-sizing</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;cite&gt;</code> — the title of a creative work (book, film, song, page). Use the font&#x27;s optical sizes (automatically pick the right cut).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;cite&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><p style="margin:0;font-size:13px">Read <cite><i>Learn HTML5</i></cite> by freeCodeCamp.</p></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;p&gt;Read &lt;cite&gt;Learn HTML5&lt;/cite&gt; by freeCodeCamp.&lt;/p&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>font-optical-sizing</b> = <b>auto</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>cite { font-optical-sizing: auto; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “The button part of &lt;input type=&quot;file&quot;&gt;.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>:</code></li><li>✔ B. <code>::file-selector-button</code></li><li>C. <code>:nth-child(n)</code></li><li>D. <code>:enabled / :disabled</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1319">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1320 / 8000 · Practice 3</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1321">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1321" data-page="1321" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 444"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 3</span><span>Page 1321 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 444 — samp × text-shadow</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">samp</span> <span class="badge prop">text-shadow</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">text-shadow</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;samp&gt;</code> — sample output from a program or computer. One or more shadows behind the text.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;samp&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><p style="margin:0;font-size:13px">If you see <samp style="font-family:monospace;background:#fef2f2;color:#b91c1c;padding:1px 5px;border-radius:4px;font-size:12px">404 Not Found</samp>, the page is missing.</p></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;p&gt;If you see &lt;samp&gt;404 Not Found&lt;/samp&gt;, the page is missing.&lt;/p&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>text-shadow</b> = <b>…</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>samp { text-shadow: …; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">Which is a valid value of box-sizing?</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>content-box</code></li><li>B. <code>solid2</code></li><li>✔ C. <code>border-box</code></li><li>D. <code>auto2</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1320">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1321 / 8000 · Practice 3</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1322">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1322" data-page="1322" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 445"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 3</span><span>Page 1322 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 445 — rp × text-orientation</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">rp</span> <span class="badge prop">text-orientation</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">text-orientation</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;rp&gt;</code> — fallback parentheses for ruby annotations in browsers without ruby support. How text rotates inside a vertical writing mode.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;rp&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="font-size:12px;font-family:serif;color:#6b7280">木(mù) — what old browsers would see</div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;ruby&gt;木&lt;rp&gt;(&lt;/rp&gt;&lt;rt&gt;mù&lt;/rt&gt;&lt;rp&gt;)&lt;/rp&gt;&lt;/ruby&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>text-orientation</b> = <b>mixed</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>rp { text-orientation: mixed; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">Which is a valid value of border-style?</p><ul class="quiz"><li>✔ A. <code>none</code></li><li>B. <code>hidden</code></li><li>C. <code>always</code></li><li>D. <code>banana2</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1321">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1322 / 8000 · Practice 3</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1323">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1323" data-page="1323" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 446"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 3</span><span>Page 1323 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 446 — dt × caret-color</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">dt</span> <span class="badge prop">caret-color</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">caret-color</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;dt&gt;</code> — the term (name) in a description list. Shorthand: width + style + color for the whole border.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;noframes&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="font-size:12px;color:#9ca3af">Frames are gone — so is <noframes>.</div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;noframes&gt;Your browser doesn&#x27;t support frames.&lt;/noframes&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>border</b> = <b>1px solid #d1d5db</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>noframes { border: 1px solid #d1d5db; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">Which is a valid value of font-style?</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>italic</code></li><li>✔ B. <code>normal</code></li><li>C. <code>banana2</code></li><li>D. <code>auto9</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1329">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1330 / 8000 · Practice 3</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1331">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1331" data-page="1331" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 454"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 3</span><span>Page 1331 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 454 — slot × clear</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">slot</span> <span class="badge prop">clear</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">clear</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;slot&gt;</code> — a placeholder in a shadow dom template where light-dom content is projected. }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">Which element is described by: “A bitmap drawing surface controlled by the 2D API or WebGL.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>&lt;tt&gt;</code></li><li>B. <code>&lt;wbr&gt;</code></li><li>C. <code>&lt;input&gt;</code></li><li>✔ D. <code>&lt;canvas&gt;</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1377">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1378 / 8000 · Practice 3</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1379">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1379" data-page="1379" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 502"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 3</span><span>Page 1379 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 502 — iframe × backface-visibility</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">iframe</span> <span class="badge prop">backface-visibility</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">backface-visibility</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;iframe&gt;</code> — embeds another html page in a nested browsing context. Hide the element when it&#x27;s rotated to show its back.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;iframe&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="border:2px solid #8b949e;border-radius:6px;width:250px;padding:8px;background:#fff"><h1 style="font-size:14px;margin:2px 0 0">Hello from an iframe</h1><div style="font-size:10px;color:#8b949e">separate document, own DOM</div></div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;iframe srcdoc=&quot;&lt;h1&gt;Hello from an iframe&lt;/h1&gt;&quot; width=&quot;260&quot; height=&quot;70&quot; sandbox=&quot;allow-same-origin&quot;&gt;&lt;/iframe&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>backface-visibility</b> = <b>hidden</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>iframe { backface-visibility: hidden; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">Which element is described by: “Embeds another HTML page in a nested browsing context.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>&lt;frameset&gt;</code></li><li>✔ B. <code>&lt;iframe&gt;</code></li><li>C. <code>&lt;details&gt;</code></li><li>D. <code>&lt;option&gt;</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1378">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1379 / 8000 · Practice 3</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1380">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1380" data-page="1380" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 503"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 3</span><span>Page 1380 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 503 — input × row-gap</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">input</span> <span class="badge prop">row-gap</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">row-gap</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;input&gt;</code> — the most versatile form control: text, email, number, date, file, checkbox, radio, range, color, search and more. Space between rows (flex lines / grid rows).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;input&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><form style="display:grid;gap:8px;font-size:12px;max-width:250px"><label style="display:grid;gap:3px"><b>Full name</b><input style="border:1px solid #d1d5db;border-radius:6px;padding:5px 8px"></label><label style="display:grid;gap:3px"><b>Email</b><input type="email" style="border:1px solid #d1d5db;border-radius:6px;padding:5px 8px"></label><label style="display:flex;gap:6px;align-items:center"><input type="checkbox" checked> Newsletter</label><button style="justify-self:start;background:#2563eb;color:#fff;border:none;border-radius:6px;padding:6px 16px">Send</button></form></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;form&gt; &lt;label&gt;Full name &lt;input type=&quot;text&quot; name=&quot;name&quot; required autocomplete=&quot;name&quot;&gt; &lt;/label&gt; &lt;label&gt;Email &lt;input type=&quot;email&quot; name=&quot;email&quot; required&gt; &lt;/label&gt; &lt;label&gt;Age &lt;input type=&quot;number&quot; name=&quot;age&quot; min=&quot;0&quot; max=&quot;120&quot;&gt; &lt;/label&gt; &lt;label&gt;&lt;input type=&quot;checkbox&quot; name=&quot;news&quot; checked&gt; Newsletter&lt;/label&gt; &lt;button&gt;Send&lt;/button&gt; &lt;/form&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>row-gap</b> = <b>length</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>input { row-gap: length; “The sole child of its parent.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>:enabled / :disabled</code></li><li>B. <code>&gt;</code></li><li>C. <code>::marker</code></li><li>✔ D. <code>:only-child</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1467">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1468 / 8000 · Practice 3</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1469">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1469" data-page="1469" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 592"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 3</span><span>Page 1469 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 592 — audio × margin-bottom</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">audio</span> <span class="badge prop">margin-bottom</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">margin-bottom</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;audio&gt;</code> — embeds an audio player (music, podcasts, sound effects). “First of its tag among siblings.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>:placeholder-shown</code></li><li>✔ B. <code>:first-of-type</code></li><li>C. <code>~</code></li><li>D. <code>::cue</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1468">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1469 / 8000 · Practice 3</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1470">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1470" data-page="1470" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 593"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 3</span><span>Page 1470 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 593 — object × border-style</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">object</span> <span class="badge prop">border-style</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">border-style</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;object&gt;</code> — embeds an external resource (legacy alternative to &lt;embed&gt;), with &lt;param&gt; children and fallback content. The line style of the border (all sides, 1–4 values).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;object&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="border:1px solid #d1d5db;border-radius:6px;width:200px;padding:10px;background:#eff6ff;font-size:11px">model.glb not supported here → fallback shows: "Download the model".</div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;object data=&quot;model.glb&quot; type=&quot;model/gltf-binary&quot; width=&quot;200&quot; height=&quot;150&quot;&gt; &lt;p&gt;Your browser cannot show 3D models. &lt;a href=&quot;model.glb&quot;&gt;Download&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/object&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>border-style</b> = <b>solid</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>object { border-style: solid; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? Vertical offset for positioned elements.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;select&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="font-size:12px"><div style="border:1px solid #d1d5db;border-radius:6px;padding:6px 10px;background:#fff;min-width:170px;display:flex;justify-content:space-between">Choose… <span style="color:#6b7280">▾</span></div><div style="border:1px solid #d1d5db;border-top:none;border-radius:0 0 6px 6px;background:#fff"><div style="padding:5px 10px;background:#eff6ff">✔ Egypt</div><div style="padding:5px 10px">Saudi Arabia</div><div style="padding:5px 10px;font-weight:600;font-size:11px;color:#6b7280">Europe</div><div style="padding:5px 10px 5px 18px">Germany</div></div></div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;select name=&quot;country&quot;&gt; &lt;option value=&quot;&quot; selected&gt;Choose…&lt;/option&gt; &lt;option value=&quot;eg&quot;&gt;Egypt&lt;/option&gt; &lt;option value=&quot;sa&quot;&gt;Saudi Arabia&lt;/option&gt; &lt;optgroup label=&quot;Europe&quot;&gt; &lt;option value=&quot;de&quot;&gt;Germany&lt;/option&gt; &lt;/optgroup&gt; &lt;/select&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>top</b> = <b>…</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>select { top: …; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Parent selector! The item&#x27;s starting main-size before grow/shrink.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;tbody&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="font-size:11px"><div style="border:1px solid #e5e7eb;padding:4px 10px">Row 1</div><div style="border:1px solid #e5e7eb;padding:4px 10px;background:#f9fafb;font-weight:600">Total</div></div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;table&gt; &lt;thead&gt;…&lt;/thead&gt; &lt;tbody&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td&gt;Row 1&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/tbody&gt; &lt;tbody class=&quot;totals&quot;&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td&gt;Total&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/tbody&gt; &lt;/table&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>flex-basis</b> = <b>length</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>tbody { flex-basis: length; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do?
